title_guess: Types of foreign investors: FDI, FPI, FII, QFI, RFPI and P-Notes

segments.teaches: foreign investors invest in India in two ways: FDI and FPI

elements.what: lavender 'foreign investors' box
red 'invest' arrow to a cream box with Indian flag
green bracket splitting into FDI and FPI

segments.notes: anchor composition (investor box -> India box) reused throughout the video

segments.teaches: FDI = buying more than 10% stake in an Indian company or setting up a factory in India

elements.what: FDI heading top-left
Walmart spark and Apple logos on the investor box
elbow arrow over the top labelled 'more than 10% stake' to a company factory icon
straight arrow labelled 'establish a manufacturing facility' to a new factory icon
blue factory and purple factory inside the India box
leader line from the company to a note on a real acquisition example

segments.notes: real company examples carry the definition (brand logos; BIE would use generic companies)

segments.teaches: why companies choose FDI: avoid customs duty, lower production cost, favourable policies

elements.what: BENEFITS label under the India box
square-bullet list growing to three items

segments.notes: list items appear one per narration beat

segments.teaches: FDI vs FPI definitions: 10%+ stake or a factory, versus financial-market investment below 10%

elements.what: anchor composition with FDI and FPI full names; FDI splits into two leaves
FPI definition under its branch

segments.notes: recap tree after the FDI detail

segments.teaches: FPI had two kinds: FII (1994, institutions, more regulation) and QFI (2011, rich individuals, less regulation), both registered with SEBI

elements.what: FPI splits into FII and QFI
year labels 1994 and 2011 with slanted pointer lines
light-blue panels describing each investor type
'register with SEBI' labels and a KYC note
red 'higher regulation' vs green 'fewer regulation' lines under each panel

segments.notes: side-by-side comparison panels with colour-coded verdict lines underneath

segments.teaches: in 2014 SEBI merged FII and QFI into one FPI category on a committee's advice

elements.what: the two panels collapse into one wide blue band covering both names
MERGED into FPI line inside the band
committee note and a blue paragraph on the effect

segments.notes: merge shown by shrinking two boxes into one band

segments.teaches: after 2014 all FPIs are called Registered FPIs (RFPI)

elements.what: FPI chip relabelled RFPI with a blue band
short circular note below

segments.notes: label swap in place rather than a new canvas

segments.teaches: RFPIs fall into three risk categories with example investor types

elements.what: RFPI -> category I / II / III -> low / medium / high risk
blue example lists under each category

segments.teaches: FPIs invest through the stock market into companies and must register with SEBI

elements.what: 'foreign investors FPI' box
stock exchange tower -> factory inside the India box
SEBI logo badge
elbow 'register' arrow from investor box to the SEBI badge

segments.notes: regulator shown as a badge sitting on the market box

segments.teaches: unregistered foreign investors can still invest through registered FPIs using participatory notes

elements.what: foreign investors split into not-registered and registered FPI
person icons (not registered) and an institution building (registered)
SEBI badges marked registered / not registered
registered FPI -> invest -> market -> company
light-blue box around the not-registered group with explanation
document icon labelled 'P NOTE'
